query: What should I focus on in this table to identify actions that could improve product scores?

per_column.name: pod_defect_quality_issue
per_column.rationale: A candidate actionable cause: presence of a product defect/quality issue plausibly drives down the product score. This is an intervenable treatment whose effect on the outcome is being attributed.

per_column.name: user_expectation_mismatch
per_column.rationale: Whether expectations were exceeded/met/mismatched sits on the causal path between an underlying product/description quality and the resulting score. It largely reflects the reviewer's evaluative judgement that produces the score rather than a common cause of a separate treatment; adjusting for it would block part of the effect. Treated as a mediator, not a confounder.

per_column.name: repeat_purchase_intent
per_column.rationale: Repurchase intent is a downstream consequence jointly determined by satisfaction/score and by product quality; conditioning on it would open spurious associations. It is an outcome-like collider, not a confounder.

per_column.name: flavor_category
per_column.rationale: Product flavor plausibly affects both the likelihood of a perceived quality/defect issue (the treatment) and the score independently (taste preferences drive ratings). As a product attribute preceding both, it is a genuine common cause that must be adjusted for. Surfaced from data, not named in the query.

judge.rationale: A plausible intervenable treatment (defect/quality issue) is present, so the treatment leg of the causal claim is met. However the confounding leg is weak: two of the added columns (expectation_mismatch, repeat_purchase_intent) are a mediator and a collider respectively -- adjusting for them would bias attribution, not correct it. Only flavor_category functions as a genuine common cause of both a quality-defect perception and the score, and even that link is only moderately plausible. No named-in-query confounders were copied, but the surfaced confounder set is thin and partly contaminated with post-treatment variables, so the causal-estimation setup is only partially realised.
